definitions.note: a card game, here the one where sevens are laid out first

parts.note: Man's number is seven, from Shakespeare's seven ages of man in As You Like It
S, for second, is a unit of time

explanation.surface: Someone too busy or too stern to sit down for a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's no' reads as a refusal, but it is 'Man's number': Shakespeare's 'seven ages of man' give SEVEN. Sevens is a card game in which runs are built outwards from the sevens.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens, also called fan-tan or domino, is a card game, so 'cards' (a game of cards) can stand for it.

clue.text: Piece of covering put up on suite finally is cream

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is turned to read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tile is one piece of a roof or floor covering

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word suite

explanation.surface: A tile is fixed above a hotel suite, which turns out to be the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses the tile because this is a down clue, where the turned word reads upwards; 'on' then places it above the closing letter of 'suite'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, its select few.

explanation.surface: Two senses of a single verb, introducing the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute is to perform a plan or order, and also to put someone to death.

parts.note: screaming in the sense of hysterical mirth, a scream of laughter

explanation.surface: A grim follow-on: kill a shrieking son.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 3-down's murder for the surface only. 'screaming' sounds like terror but means helpless mirth, as in finding something a scream.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughter means to kill, especially brutally or in large numbers.

parts.note: a party where men are deliberately not invited, held for a bride-to-be and her female friends before the wedding

explanation.surface: A grumble that the fun is happening somewhere men are not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is the British name for a bride's celebration with her women friends before the wedding, the counterpart of a stag night.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen party is a women-only celebration before a wedding, so men are absent from the fun.

indicators.note: takes means Ivan needs this extra piece to become the knight, so it is what remains once Ivan is removed

parts.note: Ivanhoe is the knight in Walter Scott's novel of that name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ivan swaps a garden implement for a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Ivan takes [this] for knight': IVAN plus the answer makes IVANHOE, Scott's knight, so the answer is what is left when IVAN is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoe is a long-handled garden tool for weeding and loosening soil.

parts.note: a sty is an enclosure for pigs

explanation.surface: Someone is calling a filthy place a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means very unpleasant or horrible.

clue.text: Charge earl with a cold first

indicators.note: first says the a and cold pieces come before the noble's title

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a count is the continental equivalent of a British earl

explanation.surface: A nobleman is charged with something while suffering a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: A and C come 'first', before COUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Charge in the sense of a bill to be settled, as in putting something on someone's account.

clue.text: Bear and male perch on tribal symbol

parts.note: to tote is to carry or bear
a pole is a measure of length also called a perch or rod

explanation.surface: A bear and a man sit atop a carved tribal emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb to carry. Pole and perch are old names for the same length, about five metres.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem pole is a carved post bearing emblems of a clan or tribe among peoples of the Pacific Northwest.

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from their job

indicators.note: clumsy suggests the letters of Teresa are handled awkwardly and come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A circus boss dismisses an awkward performer called Teresa from the juggling troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsy' turns TERESA into EATERS. The definition is loose: fire-eaters are named by the company they keep, street and circus performers alongside jugglers, with 'from' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire-eaters are circus and street entertainers of the same family as jugglers, performing tricks for a crowd.

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: extremely asks for the word tense at its extremes, its first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A sharp police officer is nervous to the utmost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but gives the element symbol CU; 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'tense', TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean shrewd or clever, as in a cute move by a canny player.

parts.note: read 'Of course' as 'of courses': a written list of the dishes or courses a restaurant offers

explanation.surface: An exasperated 'Naturally it's a list!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' sounds like 'naturally' but means 'of courses', as in the courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is the list of dishes, starter, main and dessert courses, on offer at a meal.

clue.text: My pigmy put out by stomach complaint

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small person is upset by a tummy bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MY PIGMY plus PUT. Gippy tummy is British slang for diarrhoea, especially the kind travellers pick up abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Gippy tummy is informal British slang for an upset stomach with diarrhoea, often caught on holiday.

clue.text: University in part of London is well liked

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the London district

parts.note: Poplar is a district in the East End of London

explanation.surface: A university in a London district is held in high regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U inside POPLAR, a district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular means liked or admired by many people.

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is to be judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: 'as pecked': as means when, and pecked means bitten, as by a bird

explanation.surface: Someone's face is described just after it has been bitten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as pecked', meaning when bitten, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is a side or face, as of a building or a problem.

clue.text: You may see me in store at work

definitions.text: You may see me in store at work

indicators.note: work, read as a verb, means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper says you might find them in the shop, busy at their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges IN STORE AT; the whole clue also describes a shopkeeper who sells paper and pens, seen at work in their shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a shopkeeper selling paper, pens and office supplies, whom you might see behind the counter.

clue.text: Magic liquid is back in place

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the magic drink

parts.note: a potion is a magic drink, like a love potion

indicators.note: back means the little word is is turned round to read backwards

explanation.surface: A magic elixir has been returned to where it belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses only the little word 'is', and 'in' then sets it inside the magic drink; 'Magic liquid' is a fair description of a potion, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A position is a place or location, as in taking up your post.

clue.text: Private about to enter party I have

indicators.note: to enter means the word for about goes inside the faction

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
re means about or concerning
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A private citizen joins a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts the word for 'about' inside the faction; 'Private' is an adjective here, not a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretive means inclined to keep things private or hidden.

clue.text: Ended with what's spoken of a priest

parts.note: something ended is past, over and done
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A priest's sermon brought to a close with something said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral means relating to a pastor, a minister or priest with care of a flock.

clue.text: Little swimmer's not much on a rod

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
a pole is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: A small fish caught on a fishing rod.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue one piece sitting 'on' another is placed above it; 'Little swimmer' is the definition, with 's as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the small aquatic larva of a frog, which swims with its tail.

explanation.surface: A question about which metal a police officer is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is the reddish metal element, and copper is British slang for a police officer.

clue.text: Climbing mountain endlessly, provide food to appease

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to cater is to provide food

explanation.surface: Climbers bring food to soothe someone on a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns ALP into PLA; 'endlessly' cuts the R from CATER, leaving CATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate is to calm or pacify someone who is angry.

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters could be arranged into another form

explanation.surface: A retired person's flat, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges RETIREE PAD; the whole clue is also the definition, since a small second home is just what a retiree might keep.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-a-terre is a small second home or flat kept for occasional use, a modest pad.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sultan heads off to a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To tango is to perform a particular Latin American ballroom step with a partner.

indicators.note: of here means forming part of, so the letters are taken from within the word preacher

explanation.surface: A complaint about a tiresome clergyman, the bane of a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' takes the letters sitting inside 'preacher'; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

indicators.note: goes off suggests the letters go wrong and are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Thai person leaves for an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes off' rearranges THAI into HAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean country on the western part of the island of Hispaniola.

parts.note: taken as written
FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department

explanation.surface: A question about what a civil service ministry knows.
explanation.walkthrough: The FO, or Foreign Office, is the British ministry for foreign affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Info, short for information, is what is known about something.

clue.text: Critic and I cooked up dangerous stuff?

indicators.note: cooked up means concocted, so the letters are mixed into a new form

explanation.surface: A reviewer and I have brewed something hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked up' rearranges CRITIC AND I, letters and all, 'and' included.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitric acid is a highly corrosive acid, a hazardous chemical.

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An instruction to connect something with some vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie is to fasten or join things with a knot or cord.

indicators.note: displayed means laid out on show, here with the letters of urge spread in a new order

parts.note: some can mean a few, a small number

explanation.surface: Only a handful of people show a horrible desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' rearranges URGE into GRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means horrible or grisly, causing revulsion.

clue.text: Ipecacuanha is one, and you can quote me back!

indicators.note: back says the phrase quote me is read in reverse, letter by letter

parts.note: to quote is to cite

explanation.surface: A medicine's label invites readers to repeat what it says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole phrase 'quote me', not just one word. Ipecacuanha is a plant root once widely used in syrup to induce vomiting.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance that causes vomiting, and ipecac syrup is a classic example.
